Senses.Explanation: Huike's fixed reply in the mind-settling case: ‘having sought the mind, I could not find it. Huike says his mind is not at ease; Bodhidharma tells him to bring the mind so it can be set at ease; Huike answers with this phrase; Bodhidharma replies that the mind has now been set at ease. Subsequent records repeatedly examine the quoted sentence. Yuanwu asks why Huike answered only this. Juelang distinguishes Huike's utterance from later students repeating the same words. Zhuanyu Heng explicitly judges Huike's reply as falling into conceptual understanding when comparing it with the flower sermon, while Wanfeng asks how the sentence should be understood and comments on it in another register. Daxiu Zhu redeploys the wording in a first-person public question and is immediately asked where he is now. Huigong Xiong presses the abbreviated grammar: if it is altogether unobtainable, what remains to regulate? These disagreements and questions concern the force of one fixed quoted reply; they do not create a second referent.
